newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SIAULIU SAYS HERMIS ACQUISITION NOT GUARANTEED.
newsitem.headline: SIAULIU SAYS HERMIS ACQUISITION NOT GUARANTEED.

text.p: Lithuania's Siauliu Bank said on Tuesday that it was uncertain if Hermis Bank would be able to carry out its plans to acquire a majority stake in it.
Hermis Bank was given permission earlier this month by the central bank to increase its stake in the small regional bank. It currently holds just under ten percent of Siauliu Bank's shares.
But Siauliu Bank said there was no guarantee that its current owners would part with their shares.

"Judging from the mood of the present shareholders, the majority of them do not seem to be inclined to sell their shares to Hermis Bank," Donatas Savickas, Siauliu Bank's deputy chairman, told Reuters.
"Businessmen from Siauliu would like to keep the bank as an independent regional bank," he added.
The bank begins distributing a new 14 million litas share issue tomorrow and the current shareholders have the right for one month to buy into it on a proportional basis, Savickas said.

He also said that the bank had signed a letter of intent to sell the shares not bought by current shareholders to the U.S. Baltic Fund, the Lithuanian Development Bank, and representatives of Saudi Arabia's royal family.
No shareholder currently has more than a ten percent stake in the bank, Savickas said.

A dealer with Siauliu Bank told Reuters that the issue, which will boost the bank's share capital to 34 million litas from 20 million litas, should be distributed by July and registered with the Bank of Lithuania.
Hermis Bank deputy chairman Vytautas Palijanskas told Reuters that the bank still intended to acquire a higher stake in Siauliu Bank.
Siauliu Bank's share price soared last week in the wake of the news of Hermis' intentions but it has fallen steeply over the past three sessions.
Siauliu Bank is the only regional bank to have emerged relatively unscathed from the rubble of a string of bankruptcies in 1995 and 1996 which forced many smaller banks out of business.
It had a net profit last year of 3.9 million litas after posting a loss of 2.9 million litas the previous year.
